title: I am the bread of life (John 6:35)
hookLine: the first great I am: whoever comes to me shall not hunger

lines: FIVE THOUSAND FED ON A HILLSIDE.
THEY WANT TO MAKE HIM KING.
THEY COME BACK FOR MORE BREAD.
cards: The day before, on a hillside by the Sea of Galilee, five thousand men ate from five barley loaves and two fish, with twelve baskets left over.
Then the crowd wanted to take him by force and make him king, and he slipped away. Now, the next morning, they've crossed the lake in boats to find him again.
And he tells them plainly: you're looking for me not because you saw signs, but because you ate the bread and were filled. They want more breakfast. He's about to offer them something else.

teach.b: The crowd pushes back. What sign will you give us? Our fathers ate manna in the desert; Moses gave them bread from heaven.
A fair challenge: manna fed a whole people for forty years. Jesus corrects them: it wasn't Moses who gave the bread, it's my Father who gives the true bread from heaven.

teach.h: LORD, GIVE US ALWAYS THIS BREAD.
teach.b: And they say, almost like the woman at the well: Lord, give us always this bread.
Then the line, in the Douay-Rheims: "I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall not hunger: and he that believeth in me shall never thirst."

teach.h: I AM, AND THEN A PICTURE.
teach.b: John's Gospel comes back to this shape again and again: I am, and then a picture. The light of the world. The door.
The good shepherd. The resurrection and the life. The way, the truth and the life.
The true vine. We'll meet most of them in the weeks ahead. Each takes something ordinary and says: this is what I am to you.

Bread is about as ordinary as it gets, the thing people need day after day. He's not promising they'll never miss a meal. He's speaking of a deeper hunger, the one that comes back no matter how much we eat.
Catholics hear this whole chapter as pointing toward the Eucharist, and tomorrow goes further into that.

teach.h: I AM THE BREAD OF LIFE.
teach.b: Today, stay with the plain image: bread is daily, and the promise is daily too.

how: Some Catholic families say a short grace before meals, and the Church reads John 6, the Bread of Life discourse, over several Sundays in late summer of Year B.

o: bread from heaven that fed Israel in the desert
the unleavened bread eaten at the Passover
the loaves Jesus multiplied on the hillside

games.q: the bread of life — tap the pairs.
p: not Moses but my Father gives the bread
they cross the lake to find him

s: the crowd came back because of the signs
Jesus says they came because they ate the bread and were filled.
the crowd had wanted to make Jesus king
John says they meant to take him by force, and he withdrew.
Jesus promises they'll never miss a meal
he speaks of a deeper hunger, the one food doesn't end.

games.q: you fed five thousand yesterday. today the same crowd is back, asking for a sign like the manna Moses gave. what do you give them?
o: another miracle meal, bigger than before.
yourself: I am the bread of life.
games.why: "I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall not hunger." he offers himself instead of more loaves.

practice: Before your next meal, or with food in front of you now, stop before the first bite and look at it: the hands that grew it, carried it, cooked it.

Some Catholic families say a short grace before meals, such as the old one that begins bless us, O Lord. If you pray, say it or give thanks in your own words; if not, just let the food be noticed before it's eaten.

wordCard.voice: Manna. What the crowd asked for, remembering the desert, before Jesus answered: I am the bread of life, and whoever comes to me shall not hunger. Today's word.
